title: Risks before birth
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers general health behaviours and risk factors for adolescents, not the specific risks a mother's diet, smoking and alcohol pose to a baby before birth, which is a different idea and a different depth from the Units 1 and 2 Early life content.

draft.title: Risks before birth
card: A baby's growth before birth depends on what the mother's body supplies through the placenta. What she eats, drinks and breathes in can reach the baby.
Too little folate or iron can affect development. Folate helps prevent neural tube defects, which are problems with the baby's spine and brain.
Smoking can reduce the oxygen the baby receives. It is linked to low birth weight and premature birth.
Alcohol crosses the placenta and can harm the baby's brain and body. This can cause fetal alcohol spectrum disorder. Regular antenatal check-ups and good nutrition help protect the baby.
draft.remember: What a mother takes in can reach her baby, so good nutrition and care lower the risks.

a.q: Why can a mother's smoking during pregnancy affect her baby's growth?
opts: It can reduce the oxygen the baby receives
It stops the baby from receiving any nutrients
It changes the baby's genes before birth
It makes the placenta pass on more alcohol
a.why: Smoking can reduce the oxygen that reaches the baby, which is linked to low birth weight. It does not stop all nutrients, and it does not change the baby's genes.
a.clue: Think about what the baby needs from the mother's blood besides food.

b.q: Priya is 8 weeks pregnant. Which action would best lower the risk of problems in her baby's development?
opts: Eating a balanced diet and attending antenatal check-ups
Eating much less so the baby stays small
Drinking only a small amount of alcohol each day
Avoiding all check-ups unless she feels unwell
b.why: Good nutrition and regular care protect the baby's development. Drinking alcohol can cross the placenta and harm the baby, so a small daily amount is not a safe choice.
b.clue: Look for the option that gives the baby support, not risk.

a.best: It can reduce the oxygen the baby receives

b.best: Eating a balanced diet and attending antenatal check-ups

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with the qualifier "can" and repeats the card's wording word for word. The wrong options are absolute ("any nutrients") or implausible ("more alcohol"), so a student could pick the answer without knowing the idea.
The clue "what the baby needs from the mother's blood besides food" points straight to oxygen and gives the answer away.

Every wrong option is plainly harmful (avoiding check-ups, daily alcohol, eating much less), so the question is too easy for Year 11 and tests little. The clue "support, not risk" makes it easier still.

check.summary: The facts are accurate. Question a gives itself away: the right option is the only qualified one, the distractors are weak, and the clue names oxygen. Question b's distractors are obviously harmful, making it too easy for Year 11.

proposal.title: Risks before birth
card: What a mother eats, drinks and breathes in can reach her baby through the placenta. Good nutrition and regular antenatal check-ups (health checks during pregnancy) help protect the baby.
Too little folate or iron can affect development. Folate helps prevent neural tube defects, which are problems with the baby's spine and brain.
Smoking can reduce the oxygen the baby receives. It is linked to low birth weight and premature birth.
Alcohol crosses the placenta at any stage of pregnancy and can harm the baby's brain and body, causing fetal alcohol spectrum disorder. No amount is known to be safe.
proposal.remember: Folate and iron help the baby grow. Smoking and alcohol can harm it.

a.q: Which statement about risks before birth is correct?
opts: Smoking can cut the oxygen reaching the baby
Low iron can cause fetal alcohol spectrum disorder
Iron can prevent neural tube defects in the spine
The placenta can filter alcohol out of the blood
a.why: Smoking can reduce the oxygen the baby receives, which is linked to low birth weight. Folate, not iron, helps prevent neural tube defects, and fetal alcohol spectrum disorder comes from alcohol, which crosses the placenta.
a.clue: Match each nutrient or substance to its own effect.

b.q: Priya is 8 weeks pregnant. She says a drink on weekends is fine because the placenta protects the baby. What is wrong with her reasoning?
opts: Alcohol crosses the placenta and can reach the baby
Alcohol is only a risk in the last months of pregnancy
The placenta blocks alcohol but lets nicotine through
Only heavy drinking can affect the baby's development
b.why: Alcohol crosses the placenta at any stage and can harm the baby's brain and body. Saying only heavy drinking matters is tempting, but no amount of alcohol is known to be safe in pregnancy.
b.clue: Think about what the placenta lets through, and when.
